chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Rabi' ibn Muhammad al-Musli, from Abdullah ibn Sulayman al-'Amiri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The earth has never ceased to have for God in it a Divine Authority (Hujja) who makes known the permissible and the forbidden and who invites the people to the Way of God.

key_terms.الحجة: Hujja — the Divine Proof/Authority; in Shia theology, this refers to the Imam, the infallible guide designated by God
key_terms.الحلال والحرام: The permissible and the forbidden — the domain of Islamic law which the Hujja authoritatively defines
key_terms.سبيل الله: The Way of God — the divinely ordained path of righteousness and submission

ai.seo_question: Does the earth always have a Divine Authority (Hujja) according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) affirms that the earth has never been empty of a Divine Authority (Hujja) — a guided figure appointed by God who clarifies the lawful and the unlawful and guides people to the divine path. This is a foundational creedal statement in Shia Islam establishing the necessity and continuity of the Imamate (wilayah). The original audience, students of the Imam living under Abbasid rule, would have understood this as affirming that even if the Imam is in hiding or under oppression, God's Hujja is always present on earth.
